evidence.note: Explicit layer hierarchy: stdio JSON-RPC skeleton compiled first, then a deliberate tree-sitter parse spike (test_parse.rs) to de-risk grammar before writing handlers, then symbol/handler modules, then a baseline test run as the foundation's done-check.
After 48% baseline, lists all methods with their pass rates and picks the worst/biggest buckets to attack — a prioritized method sequence chosen by cost-to-pass, not an undifferentiated push.

Sustained reprioritization across the whole horizon: repeatedly re-ranks methods by bucket size × current pass rate ('prepareCallHierarchy 55.8%, big bucket of 10890'), building later methods on validated earlier ones — the plan revisited as passing counts reveal value concentration.
Late-stage still method-by-method with concrete per-method pass checks (implementation, references, prepareCallHierarchy record fields), each fix verified via run_tests before moving on.

reasoning: The agent maintained an explicit milestone hierarchy (protocol handshake → parser spike → symbol model → prioritized per-method handlers), each with a concrete done-check (compile, parse-spike output, per-method pass rate), matching the level-8 anchor. It also exhibits level-10 traits — de-risking the riskiest grammar work early with a spike and continuously revisiting the plan as pass counts revealed where value concentrated — but the parser/symbol layers were written in one large pass rather than validated as fully separate incremental milestones, so it lands at 8 rather than a full 10.
